newsitem.title: CHINA: Inland China city to attract foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Inland China city to attract foreign investment.

text.p: The inland Chinese city of Chongqing, to be transformed into China's fourth municipality this year, has implemented tax breaks to attract foreign investment, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
Projects involving resettlement of people displaced by the Three Gorges dam across the Yangtze river will be eligible for import and income tax exemptions this year, it said.
The city has also granted exemptions to foreign-funded firms to revive its manufacturing sector, the newspaper said.

Companies with investments of at least 10 years are exempt from paying income tax for six years after becoming profitable. For the next three years they will pay just half the income tax rate and 24 percent in subsequent years, it said.
Foreign-funded firms can sell their products in China or abroad except in special government-designated cases.
Foreign-invested firms can open foreign exchange accounts in authorised banks and foreign investors are free to remit foreign exchange profits abroad, it said.
Chongqing, in southwestern Sichuan province, has attracted $1.7 billion in foreign investment.
